Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Acute asthma exacerbation with health-related anxiety
- Patient Goal(s): Relieve chest tightness; avoid hospital/intubation; feel reassured about safety
- Clinical Goal(s): Stabilise respiratory status; reduce anxiety through education and contingency planning
- Actions (Patient):
  • Commence prescribed prednisolone course as directed  
  • Resume Clenil daily and Ventolin PRN via spacer  
  • Monitor symptoms; seek medical help if Ventolin required more often than every 3 hours  
  • Practise calm breathing techniques when feeling anxious
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide e-prescriptions for Salbutamol, Clenil Modulite, spacer, and 5-day prednisolone  
  • Educate on inhaler/spacer technique and asthma action plan, including red-flag symptoms  
  • Explain possible steroid-related mood changes; advise patient to report significant shifts  
  • Offer medical certificate for rest; arrange follow-up appointment or review within one week

Secondary Problem: Medication non-adherence
- Patient Goal(s): Maintain continuous supply of inhalers
- Clinical Goal(s): Prevent future exacerbations linked to lapses
- Actions (Patient):
  • Set reminder to renew inhalers before supply runs out  
  • Keep spare inhaler set at university and home
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Arrange repeat prescriptions with pharmacy dispensing reminders  
  • Consider written asthma management plan and education resources

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Asthma triggers, inhaler/spacer use, steroid side effects, action plan for worsening symptoms
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased Ventolin use (> every 3 h), nocturnal coughing/wheezing, inability to speak full sentences, chest tightness at rest
- Coping Strategies: Pursed-lip breathing, pacing physical activity, anxiety management (slow deep breaths, reassurance of action plan)

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: To be emailed/posted (method not recorded)
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None at present
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: Within 1 week or sooner if symptoms worsen

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Anxiety/Panic Attack – Low likelihood: DDx notes chest tightness/SOB can be anxiety, but respiratory findings and asthma history are more convincing.
(Only one mental-health-related DDx identified; others not supported.)
